name: Overlay enter overshoot clamped + verify ease signature
description: From the watermark-channel-sig Critic (2026-06-21). OverlayMount.svelte visibilityStyle clamps overlay enter/exit progress to [0,1] (Math.max(0,Math.min(1,progress))), so any back.out/settled overshoot the engine computes into animState.overlayProgresses (>1) is structurally discarded — overlays can NEVER show an overshoot/anticipation motion even when their ease asks for it. Surfaces have the analogous fade-only enter (paperVisibility opacity ramp). (1) Decide: should overlays support overshoot motion (un-clamp + drive a transform, not just opacity), or is fade-through the intended overlay motion-form? The watermark identity declares fade-through, so for it the fade is correct — but the clamp is global. (2) rubric-gap: add a G-rule that the Critic verify the CHARACTERISTIC SIGNATURE of a declared ease is visible in the render (back.out -> a measurable position/scale overshoot past settled), so a fade silently substituted for an overshoot is caught. Non-gating.
result: Resolved (no engine change — clamp is correct). Investigated the OverlayMount [0,1] enter-progress clamp the watermark Critic flagged. Conclusion: it is INTENTIONAL and correct — every overlay Pipeline declares a fade-through / intrinsic motion-form (watermark explicitly 'fade-through'; counter/instance-stack/cursor-trail/shader-fill/lower-third have intrinsic motion-forms driven by mount enter timing). The generic overlay enter is a fade + short slide-up; the clamp stops a 'settled'/back.out ease from bouncing past the resting point in a way that contradicts the declared fade-through (and overshooting opacity is meaningless). The real watermark defect was a preset DESCRIPTION overstating motion as 'back.out overshoot' — already corrected to render-truth. Added a clarifying comment in OverlayMount.visibilityStyle so it isn't 'fixed' later. Enabling overshoot would be a separate per-overlay motion-form opt-in feature, not needed now. The ease-signature-verification idea is already effectively performed by Critics (the watermark Critic caught exactly this mismatch via render-is-truth).

description: The quality core. Per plane: coc = aperture * |planeZ - focusZ|; sample a DISC of radius coc (not gaussian) for bokeh; weight bright samples up so highlights bloom into bokeh discs. Surface plane (focal, CoC 0) stays sharp via the same loop (zero offset).
